newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares set high, WIG to test 16,000 Monday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares set high, WIG to test 16,000 Monday.

text.p: Polish shares set their seventh 33-month high this month on apparent foreign buying and analysts said the main market, now at 15,974.6 points, could pierce psychological resistance at 16,000 points on Monday.

"The level of 16,000 points could provide temporary psychological resistance but I think it will be beaten in the near future," said Tomasz Cwintal, an analyst at Bank Gospodarki Zywnosciowej (BGZ) brokerage.
Analysts said a good sign was that larger-cap stocks such as Bank Slaski, up 1.6 percent, were in strong demand after price-fixing on Friday.
The main market's all-share WIG index rose 0.8 percent to 15,974.6 points and turnover rose 17 percent to 180.8 million zlotys on both markets.

Four stocks rose by more than nine percent on Friday, with drug makers Polfa Kutno and Jelfa, up 9.9 percent and 9.4 percent in active trade, seen helped by anticipated good December earnings results.
Most firms release their December earnings figures on Friday and Monday. Analysts said Optimus, up 9.8 percent in heavy trade, was also helped by expectations of good seasonal earnings.

They also said Optimus' Friday surge could be linked to a newspaper article saying the firm would seek a foreign strategic investor after completing its convertible bond programme, which was progressing successfully.

Analysts said Stomil Sanok STOM.WA, which rose 9.1 percent in high turnover after starting trade on Thursday 120 percent above issue, could soon be hit by a profit-taking correction before extending gains.
NFI units fell 2.9 percent to 152.5 zlotys in a turnover of 35.9 million zlotys.
